item.title: Do you like vignettes that constantly darken the edges of the screen in a game
item.author: invalid@example.com (flyinj)
item.dc:creator: flyinj
item.content:encoded: Seeing how we probably have the most people in the world being exposed to 1/4 of their screen edge being darkened by a vignette in the game they are playing right now, I'd really like to know if anyone actually likes this. This isn't about temporary red "injured" vignettes, or "shellshocked" vignettes. This is about the "artistic choice" to constantly darken the edges of the screen. I'm going to guess this poll is going to be 85-95% no. Why do developers still do this when everyone hates it

item.title: GTA VI shows what PS5/Series X can really do. Has this gen been held back by priorities, not diminishing returns?
item.author: invalid@example.com (the_marmolade)
item.dc:creator: the_marmolade
item.content:encoded: I'm partway through GTA VI, and one thing keeps hitting me: this is the first game that genuinely feels like a generational leap on current hardware. In past generations we'd usually have seen something like this within the first couple of years of a console's life. This time it took until year six. That makes me think diminishing returns was never the issue. The headroom was there all along. Most games just didn't use it. This gen, developers have leaned hard into performance (60fps modes...
